title: What if the moon suddenly disappeared tonight?
formula: Strange act (you carry a lawn chair DOWN to the sea while 4,000 people run UP the hill, a moon-shaped hole in the sky) -> why (the moon switched off, every phone says giant wave) -> want (save Grandma's dying snack shack; Brad the realtor wants it gone) -> rival's perfect version (Brad: sandbags, floodlights, a live stream) mocks you; doubter (Mia: 'We're gonna drown') -> weird prep (Grandma's tide stick at the waterline, every light off, popcorn) -> setback (the sea pulls back, Brad: tsunami!) -> stretch (ten steps, twenty, thirty) -> explain mid-danger (bedsheet) -> undercut (a boring tide) -> stick pays off (a third) -> reversal (darkest night ever: Brad's floodlights pull every moth and blind the hill; your dark beach gets the stars) -> hidden plan revealed (lights off + popcorn = a stargazing show) -> loop: 4,000 people carry a lawn chair DOWN, and the shack sells out
loop: Line 1: you carry a lawn chair down to the ocean while 4,000 people run up the hill. Last: 4,000 people carry a lawn chair down to the ocean, straight to Grandma's popcorn.

voiceNotes.brad: Eric (ElevenLabs premade): smooth middle-aged American, a slick realtor
voiceNotes.mia: Laura (ElevenLabs premade): bright, quirky young American female, the closest premade to a 9-year-old (no child premades)

facts: Without the moon only the sun raises tides; its tidal pull is ~46% of the moon's, leaving roughly a third of today's tidal range (ScienceABC, Astronoo; ZME Science says 50-75% lower). Script: 'stops a third of the way'.

No giant wave: the moon's tidal bulge would settle like an ordinary ebb over hours, not surge (Live Science / Space.com 'what if the moon disappeared'; forum physics agrees). The bedsheet analogy is ours.
The sea pulling back from the shore is a real tsunami warning sign (Brad's line is a true fact misapplied).

Full moon ~0.25 lux vs clear moonless night with starlight + airglow ~0.002 lux: ~125x (Wikipedia 'Daylight' / 'Orders of magnitude (illuminance)'). Script: 'a hundred times darker' (vs a full-moon night).
Moonlight washes out faint stars; dark moonless skies show far more stars and the Milky Way (real). 'Exploding with stars' is comic exaggeration.
Light traps catch more insects on dark (new-moon) nights; 'every moth for fifty miles finds Brad' is comic exaggeration.
4,000 people, 500 sandbags, 50 miles: story numbers, not fact claims.

lines.narration: You carry a lawn chair down to the ocean, while 4,000 people run up the *hill*.
lines.spoken: You carry a lawn chair DOWN to the ocean, while four-thousand people run up the hill.
lines.scene: Cold open at dusk, the beach town: you walk down the beach path with a folding lawn chair, against a stream of townsfolk running uphill with flashlights, suitcases, a canoe, a grandpa hugging a TV. Behind them, over the sea, a perfect moon-shaped HOLE in the sky, ringed by a faint glow.
lines.camera: Low wide on the path, you walking toward the lens against the crowd; hard cut on '4,000' to a high wide of the hill road, a river of flashlights
lines.gag: You are the only one walking the other way; a man runs uphill carrying a canoe

lines.narration: Because the moon just switched off, and every phone in town says: giant *wave*.
lines.scene: Hard cut to a row of running faces lit by phones; every screen shows the same alert: a cartoon wave and 'NO MOON = MEGA WAVE?!'. Insert: the empty moon-shaped hole in the sky.
lines.camera: Fast push across the phone screens
lines.gag: Thirty phones flash the same giant-wave alert on thirty terrified faces

lines.narration: But you're not leaving Grandma's snack *shack*.
lines.scene: The beach: a tiny wooden snack shack, 'SHELLY'S SNACKS' sign, a giant fibreglass hot dog on the roof, Grandma's framed photo by the hatch. You snap the chair open and sit, arms crossed.
lines.camera: Low push-in on you in the chair, the shack behind
lines.gag: You snap the chair open with one flick and sit like a king guarding a castle made of hot dogs

lines.narration: It hasn't sold a hot dog in a month, and tomorrow, Brad the realtor *buys* it.
lines.scene: Insert: a cobwebbed hot dog on the grill; a 'SOLD TO BRAD - TOMORROW' sign with Brad's grinning face stuck on the shack door.
lines.camera: Macro on the cobweb, whip to the sign
lines.gag: A spider has built a web on the last hot dog

lines.narration: Brad's on the hill with 500 sandbags, two floodlights, and a live *stream*.
lines.spoken: Brad's on the hill with five-hundred sandbags, two floodlights, and a live stream.
lines.scene: Brad's hilltop fortress: a pyramid of sandbags, two blazing floodlights, Brad in a pastel suit and a bike helmet on top, phone on a selfie stick, 'LIVE 12K' on screen.
lines.camera: Telephoto from the beach up to Brad, crane up the sandbags
lines.gag: Brad poses on the sandbags like a mountaineer on a summit, selfie stick raised like a flag

lines.narration: "Enjoy the wave, chair *guy*!"
lines.speaker: brad
lines.scene: Brad points down at you for the stream; laughing emojis rain down his screen.
lines.camera: Telephoto MCU of Brad laughing, hard cut
lines.gag: Brad's face fills his own phone screen, laughing emojis raining down it

lines.narration: Even your little sister Mia thinks you've *lost* it.
lines.scene: Mia (9, two puffy pigtails, yellow raincoat, a goldfish in a bag) tugs your sleeve, the goldfish staring too.
lines.camera: Two-shot, you in the chair, Mia leaning in
lines.gag: Mia and her goldfish make the exact same worried face

lines.narration: "We're gonna *drown*."
lines.speaker: mia
lines.scene: Mia CU, eyes huge.
lines.camera: Hard cut to Mia close
lines.gag: The goldfish in her bag nods

lines.narration: You don't answer. You push Grandma's tide stick into the sand, right at the *water*.
lines.scene: You walk to the waterline and push Grandma's painted tide stick (red rings, 'SHELLY' carved on it) upright into the wet sand, right where the foam stops.
lines.camera: Macro insert: the stick sinking into the sand as foam washes round it
lines.gag: You plant it with a little twist, like a flag on the moon

lines.narration: Then you switch off every light in the *shack*.
lines.scene: Inside the shack: the fridge glow, the neon HOT DOGS sign, the string lights; you flick them off one by one.
lines.camera: Inside the hatch, hard cuts on each switch
lines.gag: The neon hot dog fizzles out last and droops

lines.narration: And you make *popcorn*.
lines.scene: A pan of popcorn pops on the camping stove; you pour it into a huge bucket and sit back down. You light one small lantern.
lines.camera: Macro on the popping pan, cut to you in the chair with the bucket
lines.gag: A kernel pops straight into your open mouth

lines.narration: Then the ocean starts pulling *back*.
lines.scene: The foam slides away from the stick, the waterline sliding down the beach, wet sand gleaming.
lines.camera: Low over the sand, pulling back with the water
lines.gag: A crab sprints after the water

lines.narration: "It pulls back before a *tsunami*!"
lines.speaker: brad
lines.scene: Brad on the sandbags, screaming at his phone; the town behind him screams too.
lines.camera: Telephoto CU of Brad, impact shake
lines.gag: Brad's helmet pops straight up off his head

lines.narration: Ten steps. Twenty. Thirty. Your stick stands in dry *sand*.
lines.spoken: Ten steps. Twenty. THIRTY. Your stick stands in dry sand.
lines.scene: The water keeps sliding away from the stick; Mia grabs your arm with both hands; you keep eating popcorn.
lines.camera: Three hard cuts, each wider: the gap between stick and water grows; end on you, bucket in your lap
lines.gag: Mia hides inside the popcorn bucket

lines.narration: You see, the moon held the ocean up in a bump, like a hand lifting a *bedsheet*.
lines.scene: Analogy mini-set: a bed in a cosy bedroom; a giant moon-white hand pinches the middle of the blue bedsheet and lifts it into a hump.
lines.camera: Dissolve in; push in on the hump
lines.gag: A tiny toy boat rides on top of the bedsheet hump

lines.narration: Let go, and the sheet doesn't *slam*. It just... settles.
lines.scene: The hand vanishes; the sheet sinks flat, the toy boat gently lowering with it. Match cut to the bay, flat and calm.
lines.camera: Slow tilt down with the sheet, match cut to the bay
lines.gag: The toy boat lands without spilling a drop

lines.narration: No wave. Just a slow, boring *tide*.
lines.scene: The bay lies flat; the tiniest wave in history flops onto the sand at your feet.
lines.camera: Wide hold on the calm bay, you and Mia small in the foreground
lines.gag: The tiniest wave in history flops onto the beach

lines.narration: When your lantern burns down, the water crawls back... and quits a third of the way to your *stick*.
lines.scene: Time passing in one place, no card: the lantern candle shrinks to a stub, the popcorn bucket empties, Mia falls asleep on your shoulder; the tide creeps back and stops far short of the stick, a dark wet line a third of the way up the beach.
lines.camera: Match-framed dissolve on the lantern, then low along the sand from the stick to the stopped waterline
lines.gag: The foam reaches toward the stick and gives up, like it's out of breath

lines.narration: But the moon was the world's biggest nightlight. Without it, the night goes a hundred times *darker*.
lines.scene: Wide of the whole bay: the town goes inky black; only Brad's floodlights blaze on the hill.
lines.camera: Fast pull-out to the widest shot of the video
lines.gag: Brad's hill is the only lit thing in the world, like a birthday cake in a dark room

lines.narration: So Brad's floodlights are the brightest thing for fifty miles, and every moth for fifty miles finds *Brad*.
lines.spoken: So Brad's floodlights are the brightest thing for fifty miles, and every moth for fifty miles finds BRAD.
lines.scene: A huge cloud of moths swirls into the floodlights and over Brad; his stream shows only moths; the crowd on the hill squints into the glare.
lines.camera: Telephoto push on Brad disappearing into moths
lines.gag: Brad's live stream is 100 % moth

lines.narration: Up there, nobody sees a thing. But on your dark beach, the sky *explodes* with stars.
lines.scene: Tilt up from you, Mia and the lantern stub to the Milky Way blazing over the sea; on the hill, the crowd turns from the moth storm and stares down at your beach.
lines.camera: Low angle tilt up from your faces to the star-packed sky
lines.gag: Mia's mouth drops open so wide a popcorn kernel falls in; her goldfish looks up too

lines.narration: So 4,000 people carry a lawn chair down to the ocean, straight to Grandma's *popcorn*.
lines.spoken: So four-thousand people carry a lawn chair DOWN to the ocean, straight to Grandma's popcorn.
lines.scene: Mirror of the opening: the whole town walks DOWN the beach path with lawn chairs; the shack hatch is open, a queue to the dunes, a 'SOLD OUT' card slapped on the popcorn. End on your smug face, the chairs and stars blurred behind; a moth-covered Brad in the queue holding a chair.
lines.camera: Mirror of the opening low wide, then a CU of your smug face
lines.gag: A sea of lawn chairs; moth-covered Brad waits in the popcorn line
